Mechwarrior: Dark Age Official Campaign Fiction
 
 
INTRODUCTIONS
 
Mechwarrior Dark Age and later Mechwarrior Age of Destruction was a short
-
lived (2002
-
2008) miniatures game by Wizkids Games, created by Jordan Weis-man, the original creator of Battletech. It was a re—imagining of the Battletech game, with pre
-
 painted miniatures that came in random
-
sorted boosters Jordan Weisman wanted to return the Battletech setting to a
‘3025’
atmosphere, where
‘
Mechs were rare and the fate of an entire planet could revolve around a single lance. He also wanted to introduce more of a
‘
combined
-
arms
’
style of combat. During its heyday, Mechwarrior Dark Age was one of the most popular minis games on the market, with thousands of tournaments weekly and huge showings at GenCon. The game is still beloved by many fans who have kept it alive, over a decade since Wizkids
’
then
-
owner Topps, ordered them to shutter most of their minis games amid the 2008 Financial Crisis. One of the things that made Mechwarrior Dark Age such a lively scene, especially early on, was the opportunity for players to affect the universe directly through tournaments. From 2002 to about 2005, Wizkids set up weekly tournaments where  players could determine the fates of planets as two splinter factions from the Re- public went to war over them. Wizkids would then update a map of the Republic of the Sphere on their website to show the current conquests of each faction. The tournaments also came with short fiction pieces for each faction involved, as they fought the battles out that real
-
life players were affecting. Add in lots of prize sup- port, and you had players hooked.
 
I got into Mechwarrior personally right as the in
-
depth storylines and prizes were  petering around (Around 2005), but as a young kid with a love for fiction, I con-stantly poured over all the stories again and again on the Wizkids website. When the original Wizkids website went defunct, many of the stories and articles were saved and moved over as PDFs to the main Battletech website, but one thing that was missed was all the campaign fiction pieces. Using WaybackMachine to find screenshots, I have compiled every campaign story I could find into this document. I hope you will find these stories as enjoyable to read now as they were for me as a teen.
 
SEYLA!
 
Sincerely,
 
James Hojnowski
 
(Captain of C
-
21/James Bedford)
 
((Spirits Cats are the best!))
 
 
HOW TO USE THIS BOOK:
 
Each campaign was between 2
-
4 weeks, with fiction each week. Starting with the Archenar campaign, Wizkids also started writing a short summary of who won each week, and why. Planets were won typically by the faction that won the final week campaign. There are also  brief blurbs over why the campaign is being fought, and when appropriate, I have included the  brief description
Era Digest: Dark Age
wrote up about the campaign at the end. I also added at the end 4 short story pieces that Wizkids had several longtime Battletech au-thors write to introduce the Dark Age game. These stories technically occur BEFORE all of the campaigns chronologically, but I started this document just for the campaigns, and added them for completion
’
s sake. If you like reading things chronologically, read
“
Inheritance of Duty
”, “
Angry Voices in the Dark 
”,
and
“
Field to Field
”,
then go back to the campaigns.
